response_text: First the user creates a thread by calling the osCreateThread() function and passes both a function pointer and the argument. The argument is often passed as a pointer to some data. The OS then prepares a stack for the new thread. During the stack setup, the OS stores the arguments to be passed in the r0 register. This will be stored when the thread first runs. When the scheduler switches to the new thread, the CPU loads the arguments from the stack into R0, so calling when the thread function starts it receives the argument as intended. The argument is particularly loaded into R0 because of the Crotex-M calling convention, which expects the first argument to be in R0.\n
